findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the management port.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised instance unrestricted outbound communication for data exfiltration or C2 traffic.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in the EC2 user_data script; user_data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the host (or via SSRF), leaking long-lived credentials.
No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and the credentials/metadata endpoint can be reached through SSRF against the web server.
The instance does not specify root_block_device encryption, so the root EBS volume may store data unencrypted at rest.
The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a route to the internet gateway, making it directly reachable from the internet along with its wide-open SSH port.
The EBS volume has no encrypted = true setting, so the attached data disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so backup data is also stored unencrypted and could be exposed if the snapshot is shared or leaked.
The VPC flow log S3 bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving sensitive network telemetry unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy restriction is configured for the flow log bucket, risking accidental public exposure of network logs.
The bucket lacks versioning and server access logging, so tampering with or deletion of flow log evidence would be unrecoverable and undetectable.
force_destroy = true allows the audit/flow-log bucket and all its objects to be deleted without protection, undermining log integrity and retention.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, automatically expanding internet-facing attack surface.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, automatically expanding internet-facing attack surface.
The VPC does not restrict its default security group (no aws_default_security_group resource), so resources launched without an explicit SG may inherit permissive default rules.
